evidence.title: Affect in the archive: trauma, grief, delight and texts. Some personal reflections
evidence.author: Russell, Lynette
excerpts: Some personal reflections | Archives & Manuscripts Skip to main content Skip to main navigation menu Skip to site footer Affect in the archive: trauma, grief, delight and texts.
We can form romantic attachments or be repulsed across the decades.
Archives containing the physical remains of the past can transport us, we can move beyond the here and now.
Before the Museum of Melbourne digitised Alfred Howitt’s correspondence, I once opened a letter written to him on classic nineteenth-century blued paper.
As I pulled the missive from its envelope, I could smell tobacco smoke.

Recently, after completing an article on the topic of frontier violence, my co-author and I both described a feeling of stress and trauma that came from reading colonial records of ‘skirmishes’ and ‘dispersals’.
In this paper, I want to reflect on the experience of Affect in the archive.
(2018) “Affect in the archive: trauma, grief, delight and texts.
Some personal reflections”, Archives & Manuscripts , 46(2), pp.

About the Journal Archives and Manuscripts is the professional and scholarly journal of the Australian Society of Archivists , publishing articles, reviews, and information about the theory and practice of archives and recordkeeping in Australasia and around the world.
Its target audiences are archivists and other recordkeeping professionals, the academic community, and all involved in the study and interpretation of archives.
